item.title: Tropical Depression Edouard Public Advisory Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 1000 PM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026 
000
WTNT35 KNHC 020231
TCPAT5
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Edouard Advisory Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL052026
1000 PM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026
 
...EDOUARD WEAKENS TO A DEPRESSION...
...GUSTY WINDS AND HEAVY RAINFALL CONTINUE SPREADING OVER
SOUTHEASTERN TEXAS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1000 PM CDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...30.5N 94.6W
ABOUT 40 MI...65 KM NW OF BEAUMONT TEXAS
ABOUT 50 MI...80 KM SSE OF LUFKIN TEXAS
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 315 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The Tropical Storm Warning has been discontinued along the Texas ad
Louisiana coasts.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1000 PM CDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Edouard
was located near latitude 30.5 North, longitude 94.6 West. The
depression is moving toward the northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h), and
this motion is expected to continue for the next day or so. On the
forecast track, the center of Edouard will continue moving inland
over southeastern and eastern Texas through Wednesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 35 mph (55 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Continued weakening is expected during the next
day or so, and Edouard is forecast to weaken to a tropical
depression tonight and dissipate by Wednesday night.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Tropical Storm Edouard can be found in the
Tropical Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDAT5 and WMO
header WTNT45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Wind gusts to tropical-storm force may continue near the
center of Edouard for the next several hours.
 
RAINFALL: Edouard is expected to produce rainfall totals of 3 to 7
inches with maximum totals up to 12 inches for parts of the Upper
Texas Coast inland through east-central Texas, with potential for 2
to 4 inches in far southwest Louisiana. This rainfall is likely to
produce flash flooding, especially in low-lying and urban areas.
Significant flash flooding is possible. River flooding may also be
possible.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Edouard, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total
Rainfall Graphic available at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_at5.shtml?rainqpf and the Flash Flood Risk
graphic at hurricanes.gov/graphics_at5.shtml?ero.
 
For a list of rainfall observations (and wind reports) associated
with Edouard, see the companion storm summary at WBCSCCNS5 with the
WMO header ACUS45 KWBC or at the following link:
www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/discussions/nfdscc5.html.
 
TORNADOES: A tornado or two is possible through tonight across
parts of southwest Louisiana and southeast Texas.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane
Center on this system. Future information on this system can be 
found in Public Advisories issued by the Weather Prediction Center 
beginning at 400 AM CDT, under AWIPS header TCPAT5, WMO header 
WTNT35 KWNH, and on the web at www.hurricanes.gov.

Rainfall forecasts for the United States can always be found at 
https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/qpf2.shtml 
and outlooks of flash flood risks can be found at 
https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/excessive_rainfall_outlook_ero.php
.

$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Tropical Depression Edouard Forecast Discussion Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 1000 PM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026 
000
WTNT45 KNHC 020232
TCDAT5
 
Tropical Depression Edouard Discussion Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL052026
1000 PM CDT Tue Sep 01 2026

Edouard has remained well-organized in radar imagery as it moves 
farther inland over southeastern Texas. However, the convective 
cloud tops near the center are gradually, if unsteadily warming, 
and Doppler wind velocities near the center have decreased during 
the last hour or so. Based on this, it is estimated that Edouard 
has weakened to a tropical depression. It should be noted that 
there have been no reports of winds or pressures from the storm 
core area after it passed Beaumont, Texas.

Continued weakening is expected as the center moves farther inland, 
and the dynamical guidance suggests that the surface center should 
dissipate between 18-36 h. The intensity forecast thus calls for 
the system to last 24 h before dissipation. 

Edouard is moving northwestward or 315/7 kt and will remain on this 
heading through early Wednesday, bringing the center farther inland 
over eastern Texas. This general motion should continue until the 
surface center dissipates.

This is the last tropical cyclone discussion issued by the National 
Hurricane Center on this system.  Future information on this system 
can be found in discussions issued by the Weather Prediction Center 
beginning at 400 AM CDT, under AWIPS header TCDAT5, WMO header 
WTNT45 KWNH, and on the web at www.hurricanes.gov.

Rainfall forecasts for the United States can always be found at 
https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/qpf2.shtml 
and outlooks of flash flood risks can be found at 
https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/qpf/excessive_rainfall_outlook_ero.php
.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Wind gusts to tropical-storm force are likely near the center of 
Edouard for the next several hours.
 
2. Heavy rain will impact parts of the Upper Texas coast through 
east-central Texas into far Southwest Louisiana through Thursday 
morning as Edouard continues to track inland. Flash flooding is 
likely across this region, especially in urban areas. Significant 
flash flooding is possible. River flooding may also be possible.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  02/0300Z 30.5N  94.6W   30 KT  35 MPH...INLAND
 12H  02/1200Z 31.2N  95.4W   25 KT  30 MPH...INLAND
 24H  03/0000Z 32.2N  95.9W   20 KT  25 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 36H  03/1200Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Beven
